chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, and Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, all from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Basir, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
Humran asked him, 'May Allah make me a ransom for you! If you were to narrate to us when this Matter will occur, it would make us happy.'

He said, 'O Humran! You have friends, brothers, and acquaintances. There was a scholar in the past who had a son who was not interested in his father's knowledge and did not ask him about anything. He had a neighbor who would come to him, ask him, and take knowledge from him. When death approached the man, he called his son and said, 'O my son! You have shown disinterest in what I have, your desire for it is low, and you never asked me about anything. I have a neighbor who used to come to me, ask me, take from me, and memorize from me. So if you need anything, go to him.' He introduced his neighbor to him. The man died, and his son remained.

The king of that era saw a dream and asked about the man. It was said to him, 'He has died.' The king said, 'Did he leave a son?' It was said, 'Yes, he left a son.' The king said, 'Bring him to me.' They were sent to him to bring him to the king. The boy said, 'By Allah, I do not know why the king is calling me, and I have no knowledge. If he asks me about something, I will be disgraced.' He remembered what his father had bequeathed to him, so he went to the man who used to take knowledge from his father. He said to him, 'The king has sent for me to ask me, and I do not know what he has sent for me. My father had ordered me to come to you if I needed anything.'

The man said, 'But I know what he has sent for you. If I inform you, then whatever Allah brings out to you, it will be between you and me.' He said, 'Yes.' He took an oath from him and made a binding agreement that he would be loyal. The boy made a binding agreement with him. He said, 'He wants to ask you about a dream he saw, as to which era it is. So say to him, 'This is the era of the wolf.''

The boy went to him. The king said to him, 'Do you know why I sent for you?' He said, 'You sent for me intending to ask me about a dream you saw, as to which era it is.' The king said, 'You speak the truth, so inform me which era this is.' He said to him, 'The era of the wolf.' So he ordered an award for him, and the boy took it and returned to his house. He refused to be loyal to his companion.

He said, 'Perhaps I will not exhaust this wealth, nor consume it until I die, and perhaps I will not need him, nor be asked about something like this which I was asked about.' So he remained for as long as Allah willed.

Then the king saw a dream and sent for him, calling him. He regretted what he had done and said, 'By Allah, I have no knowledge to give him, and I do not know how to deal with my companion, and I have betrayed him and not been loyal to him.' Then he said, 'I will go to him in any case, and I will excuse myself to him, and I will swear to him, perhaps he will inform me.' So he went to him and said, 'I have done what I have done, and I have not been loyal to you for what was between us, and what was in my hand has gone, and I have need of you. So I adjure you by Allah not to abandon me, and I make a binding agreement with you that nothing will be given to me except that it will be between you and me. The king has sent for me, and I do not know what he will ask me about.'
He said, 'He wants to ask you about a dream he saw, as to which era it is. So say to him, 'This is the era of the ram.''

He went to the king and entered upon him. The king said, 'Why did I send for you?' He said, 'You saw a dream and you want to ask me which era this is.' The king said to him, 'You speak the truth, so inform me which era this is.' He said, 'This is the era of the ram.' So he ordered a gift for him, and he took it and returned to his house. He pondered in his mind whether to be loyal to his companion or not. Sometimes he thought to do it, and sometimes he thought not to do it. Then he said, 'Perhaps I will not need him after this time ever,' and he decided on betrayal and leaving loyalty. So he remained for as long as Allah willed.

Then the king saw a dream and sent for him. He regretted what he had done between himself and his companion and said, 'After betraying him twice, how shall I act, and I have no knowledge?' Then he decided on going to the man. He went to him and adjured him by Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and asked him to teach him, and informed him that this time he would be loyal to him and made a binding agreement with him, saying, 'Do not leave me in this state, for I will not return to betrayal, and I will be loyal to you.' He made a binding agreement with him. He said, 'He is calling you to ask you about a dream he saw, as to which era it is. When he asks you, inform him that it is the era of the scale.'

He said, 'So he went to the king and entered upon him. The king said to him, 'Why did I send for you?' He said, 'You saw a dream and you want to ask me which era this is.' He said, 'You speak the truth, so inform me which era this is.' He said, 'This is the era of the scale.' So he ordered a gift for him, and he took it and went with it to the man. He placed it before him and said, 'I have come to you with what was given to me, so divide it with me.''

The scholar said to him, 'The first era was the era of the wolf, and you were from the wolves. The second era was the era of the ram, which thinks but does not act, and so you were thinking but not being loyal. This era was the era of the scale, and you were upon loyalty. So take your wealth, for I have no need for it,' and he returned it to him.
ai.seo_question: What is the story of the scholar's son and the three eras in Kafi?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Baqir (as) uses the parable of the scholar's son to illustrate the spiritual states of the community across three eras: the 'Era of the Wolf' (aggression), the 'Era of the Ram' (hesitation), and the 'Era of the Scale' (balance and fidelity). The son’s progression from betrayal to loyalty mirrors the expected conduct of the faithful, emphasizing that true success lies in maintaining trust (*amanah*) and fulfilling covenants with knowledge bearers.

en.hubeali: H 14999 – Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Abu Ali Al-Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, together from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, who has narrated the following: Abu Ja’farasws said, ‘Humran asked himasws, ‘May Allahazwj Make me to be sacrificed for youasws! If youasws were to narrate to us when this Matter (Al-Qaimasws) is to take place, it would make us happy’. Heasws said: ‘O Humran! You have friends, and brothers, and people whom you know. There used to be a scholar in the past, and he had a son who was never interested in the knowledge of his father, and did not ask him about anything, and they had a neighbour who used to come over and ask him, and take (knowledge) from him. The death presented itself to the man, so he called his son and said, ‘O my son! You have kept yourself away from what was in my possession, and had very little interest in it, and you never used to ask me about anything, whilst I had a neighbour who used to come to me, and ask me, and take (knowledge) from me, and memorise it from me. So now if you ever need anything, go to him. He introduced his neighbour to him. The man died, and his son remained. The king of that era saw a dream, so he asked around for the man. It was said to him that he had died. So the king said, ‘Did he leave a son?’ It was said to him, ‘Yes, he left a son’. So he said, ‘Bring him to me’. They went to him in order to bring him to the king. The boy said, ‘By Allahazwj, I do not know why the king has called me, and there is no knowledge with me, and if he were to ask me about something, I would be disgraced’. He remembered what his father has bequeathed to him, so he came to the man who used to take the knowledge from his father. He said to him, ‘The king has sent for me to ask me, and I do not know why he has sent for me, and my father had ordered me that I should come to you if I ever have a need for anything’. The man said, ‘But I know very well with regards to what he has sent for you. So, if I were to inform you, then whatsoever that Allahazwj Brings out to you, so it would be (divided) between you and me’. He said, ‘Yes’. He took an oath from him and made a binding agreement with the boy. He said, ‘He wants to ask you about a dream that he saw, as to which era it relates to? So you should say to him, ‘This is the era of the wolf’. The boy went to him, and the king said to him, ‘Do you know why I sent for you?’ He said, ‘You sent for me intending to ask me about a dream that you saw, as to which era it relates to’. The king said, ‘You speak the truth, so inform me as to which era it relates to’. He said to him, ‘The era of the wolf’. So he ordered for an award to be given to him, and the boy grabbed it and left to go to his house. He refused to be loyal to his companion and said (to himself), ‘I will not hand over this wealth, and will consume it until I die, and there is no need for me, nor will I ever have to ask him about anything similar to what I have already asked him’. So that (situation) prevailed for as long as Allahazwj Desired it to. Then the king saw (another) dream, so he sent for the boy. He regretted at what he had done and said, ‘By Allahazwj, there is no knowledge with me that I can give, and I do not know how to deal with my companion, and I have betrayed him, and never apologised to him’. Then said, ‘Let me go to him in any case and present excuses to him, hopefully he will inform me’. So he came and said to him, ‘I have done what I have done, and never apologised to you for what happened between I and you, and that which was in my hands has gone, and I have now got a need from you’. So adjure me to Allahazwj and do not abandon me, and I am a reliable one for you, that nothing will be given to me except that it would be (divided) between you and me. And the king has sent for me and I do not know what he will be asking me’. So he said, ‘He intends to ask you about a dream he saw, as to which era it relates to, so say to him, ‘It is for the era of the ram’. So he went to the king who said, ‘Do you know why I have sent for you?’ He said, ‘You saw a dream and you want to ask me as to which era it relates to’. So he said to him, ‘You have spoken the truth, so tell me which era this is for?’ He said, ‘This is for the era of the ram’. So he ordered a reward for him. The boy grabbed it and left for his house, and he was pondering whether he should be loyal to his companion, or whether he should not be loyal to him. Sometimes he thought that he should do it, sometimes he thought that he should not do it. Then he said (to himself), ‘I will have no need for him anymore after this time ever’, and opted for the betrayal and leave the loyalty. So that (situation) prevailed for as long as Allahazwj Desired it to. Then the king saw (another) dream, so he sent for him. He regretted at what he had done regarding what was between himself and his companion and said (to himself), ‘I have betrayed him twice, how shall I face him, and there is no knowledge with me. Then he decided on going to the man, and came up to him. So he swore upon Allahazwj Blessed and High, and asked him to let him know and inform him, and that this time he would be loyal to him, and be a trustworthy to him, and said, ‘Do not leave me upon this condition, for I will not return to the betrayal, and will be loyal to you. So he took an agreement from him. He said, ‘He has called you to ask you about a dream he saw, as to which era it relates to. So when he questions you, inform him that it is for the era of the scale (balance)’. Heasws said: ‘So he came up to the king who said to him, ‘Do you know why I have sent for you?’ He said, ‘You have seen a dream and intend to ask me as to which era it relates to’. He said, ‘You have spoken the truth, so tell me which era this is for?’ He said, ‘This is for the era of the scale’. So he ordered a reward for him. The boy grabbed the reward and went with it to the man and placed it in front of him and said, ‘I have come to you with whatever was given to me, so divided it equally’. So the scholar said to him, ‘The first period was like the era of the wolf, and you were from the wolves. And the second period was the era of the ram which thinks but does not do it, and similarly you were thinking about it but were not loyal. And this period is the era of the scale, and you were, with regards to it, upon the loyalty. So grab your wealth for I have no need for it’. And he returned it back to him’.
en.sarwar: 553. Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Ahmad Al-Kufy, from Ali Bin Al-Hassan Al-Taymi, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Ali Bin Ja’far who said, ‘Narrated to me Moattab, or someone else, who said: ‘Abdullah Bin Al-Hassan sent a message to Abu Abdullah (a.s.) saying, ‘Abu Muhammad says to you (a.s.), ‘I am braver than you (a.s.), and I am more generous than you (a.s.), and I am more knowledgeable than you (a.s.)’.
So he (a.s.) said to his messenger: ‘As for the bravery, by Allah (azwj) there has not been an incident whereby your cowardice can be distinguished from your bravery.
And as for the generosity, so it is taking something and placing it in its rightful place.
And as for the knowledge, your forefather Ali (a.s.) Bin Abu Talib (a.s.) had freed a thousand slaves, therefore name five of them for us (a.s.) if you are a knowledgeable one’.
So the messenger returned to him.
He told him, then he returned back to him (a.s.) saying, ‘He is saying to you (a.s.), that you (a.s.) are a man of Books’.
So Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said to him; ‘Tell him, ‘Yes, by Allah (azwj), the Books of Ibrahim (as), and Musa (as), and Isa (as), which I (a.s.) have inherited from my (a.s.) forefathers (a.s.)’.
